# The Unmooring
[italic]Nobody agrees on what it is. Everybody agrees on where it starts.[/italic]
Since [textlink="the Collapse" link="WFLoreCollapse"], the further a ship flies from the sector's heart, the less the world agrees with itself. Clocks aboard drift apart. Instruments report things that were never there, then deny it. Spacers call it [color=#d070ff]the Unmooring[/color], because that is what it feels like: the moment a ship slips its line and begins to turn with the current.
What holds it back is [textlink="the Lattice" link="WFLoreLattice"]. What lies beyond the Lattice's reach is a matter of record only in the sense that some of it was recorded.
## The charts
Every navigation computer in the sector carries the same warnings, and nobody remembers writing them. They mark the space past roughly eighteen kilometres as restricted, and they name its depths:
- [color=#e0b040]Detune[/color]. - [color=#e08030]Dissonance[/color]. - [color=#e04030]Feedback[/color]. - [color=#d030a0]the C#d#[/color]. The charts have never printed the last name cleanly. Technicians have replaced the charts. The name still comes out wrong.
## From the record
[italic]Salvage log, MSV Harrow, partial. Recovered from a drifting hull at 27 km.[/italic]
"Day four out. Wren swears she heard Okafor calling from the cargo bay. Okafor is on the bridge with me. We checked the bay anyway. Nobody. The vents were warm."
"Day five. Scope shows a contact three hundred metres off the bow. Matching our speed. Pinged it. Nothing pinged back. It's still there when I look away."
"Day six. The cat is gone. Okafor says there never was a cat. I remember the cat."
[italic]The rest of the log is the same sentence, written eleven hundred times. It has not been translated.[/italic]
## What people say
- That the longer you stay out, the more it [bold]takes[/bold]. Crews call it Drift, the way a ship drifts, and it does not leave when you do. It fades. Slowly. - That nobody sees the same thing. Two crewmen side by side, one screaming at a figure in the corridor, the other seeing an empty corridor. - That small minds go first. Pets. Vermin. [italic]That they get back up.[/italic] - That the rock out there is richer than anything in the inner sector, and that it holds [color=#d070ff]exotic matter[/color], which should not exist and is worth more than the ship that carries it. - That some who go deep come back humming. See [textlink="the Choir" link="WFLoreChoir"].
